title: Biased randomized computation beyond computability
statement: There exist a real number $\rho$ with $0\le \rho\le 1$ and a language $L$ of bit strings that is not computable, yet belongs to the bounded-error polynomial-time class using independent random bits that equal $1$ with probability $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: The bias parameter $\rho$ lies between $0$ and $1
Membership of $L$ in the biased bounded-error polynomial-time class at bias $\rho$
The predicate for membership in $L$ is not computable
